title: Wave 3 open decisions: commit email and dashboard scope
intro: ANSWERED 2026-11-15, applied: D1 keep-history-redact-text (keep the history, no force push); D2 placeholder-for-1a (plain page with a usage view in 1a, React moves to 1b). The cards below show the question as it was asked, so D2's context still says the page has no usage view; it has one now. See wave3-open-decisions.md. Original intro: D1 to D3 of wave 3 are applied and not asked again. PR #43 (Codex adapter, two calls under D7) is on its own page, docs/reviews/pr43-codex-decisions.html; answer it there. Two calls remain here. Module 6B, module 16, the integration tests and the tutorial wait on the 6B pull request from the factory-40 session, not on you, except the dashboard parts of the tutorial (D2 below).

decisions.title: Your work email in commit 6a6ff04
decisions.ref: docs/tasks.md item 8 and the 2026-11-14 final-pass log; git history of main
decisions.context: Commit 6a6ff04 has your work email as its author, and the public GitHub API returns it for that commit. 44 of the 45 pull request heads on GitHub contain the commit, and 73 commits sit after it on main (77 in all). No fork exists. docs/tasks.md also holds the address as text; that text is removed in this same change, with no force push. New commits carry no email at all: 55 commits on main have an empty author email, and this repo's git config sets none. Removing the commit itself needs a force push of main, which you have not approved. GitHub's own guide says a rewrite does not clear its pull request refs, and only GitHub Support can.

options.name: Keep the history as it is. The text copy in docs/tasks.md is already removed. No force push
pros: Matches your earlier choice B on authorship: keep current authors, no history rewrite
No SHA changes, so the 45 remote branches, the 21 local worktrees and open PR #43 stay valid
Reversible: you can still choose a rewrite later
cons: The address stays readable on that one commit through the GitHub API and git log, and in every clone made so far
A rewrite gets dearer as history grows: it already touches 73 commits, and GitHub Support is still needed for the PR refs
If the address is a risk to you, this option does nothing for it

options.name: Rewrite the history to replace the email, force-push every branch, then ask GitHub Support to purge the pull request refs
pros: The only way to remove the address from this repository for good
Done now, it touches 73 commits, not more
cons: Needs your approval for force pushes, and breaks the standing rule not to force push
Every commit after 6a6ff04 gets a new SHA: 73 on main, plus the 45 remote branches and open PR #43, which the other sessions must rebase
The PR refs keep the old commit until GitHub Support acts, and a PR body can keep the address even then (GitHub's guide)
git-filter-repo is not installed on this machine, so a tool must be added first

options.name: Start a clean repository from a squashed copy of main, then delete or make private the old one
pros: No Support request and no force push: the new history never held the address
Zero forks and zero stars today, so nobody else depends on the old repository
cons: Loses the 45 pull requests, their review comments and the per-commit history the decision logs cite
Open PR #43 and every other session's branch must be moved by hand, and the repository URL changes
The address is gone only if the old repository is deleted or made private, which is your call and not reversible once deleted

decisions.why: You already chose to keep current authors, the text copy is gone, and a rewrite can still be done later; the cost of waiting is that the address stays on one commit.

decisions.title: Dashboard in phase 1a: placeholder page or React bundle
decisions.ref: Module 15; phase-1.md Dashboard rows (phase split and Tech choices); AGENTS.md factory/dashboard; tasks.md item 6
decisions.context: The spec says React, shipped as a prebuilt bundle. Module 15 merged with a 296-line plain HTML placeholder at factory/dashboard/index.html. It shows Needs you, the runs overview, run detail and Show JSON. It has no usage view, although the server returns usage in run detail. The repo holds no React source (no package.json, no .jsx or .tsx files). The module 15 criteria for the page (refresh, Needs you buttons, run detail paths) are unticked until a UI test runs. The tutorial's dashboard section depends on this.

options.name: Phase 1a ships the placeholder page, with a usage view added. The React bundle moves to phase 1b
pros: The pilot needs a read-only page, and the placeholder already does that
Unblocks the tutorial and the UI tests now, with no new build chain
Spec change is small: one row in the phase split table and one criterion note
cons: The spec says React for the dashboard, so phase 1a ships something other than what the spec describes
UI tests written for the placeholder markup need rewriting when React lands

options.name: Build the React source and its bundle before phase 1a closes
pros: Matches the spec as written; no spec change
UI tests are written once, against the real page
Node 26.13.0 is installed here, so a build is possible
cons: Starts from nothing: there is no React source in the repo
Adds a build step and a bundle to the kit, and delays the tutorial
Spends phase 1a time on UI polish, not on the engine path the pilot proves

options.name: Make the plain page the dashboard and drop React from the spec
pros: No build step or Node needed to serve the dashboard
One page to test, with the UI tests written once
The spec and the code agree
cons: Reverses a decision in the phase 1 spec, so it needs a new ADR
Phase 1b writes (Submit, notes, retry, goto, skip, abort) are harder to build as hand-written markup
Gives up the designed UI the spec promises

decisions.why: The pilot is read-only and the engine path matters more; the placeholder covers it now and React can follow in 1b without redoing the server.
